cli.usage:
usage: mcp-n4 [-h] [--allow-writes] [--write-scope ORD_PREFIX]
              [--state-dir STATE_DIR] [--token-ttl SECONDS] [--max-writes N]
              [--auth-cooldown SECONDS] [--load-wait SECONDS]
              [--http-timeout SECONDS] [--station NAME=URL]
              [--station-home NAME=PATH] [--niagara-home NAME=PATH]
              [--credential-env PREFIX] [--insecure-tls NAME]
              [--allow-tier-b NAME] [--allow-tier-c NAME]
              [--progress-file PATH] [--allow-http-for-tests]
cli.help:
usage: mcp-n4 [-h] [--allow-writes] [--write-scope ORD_PREFIX]
              [--state-dir STATE_DIR] [--token-ttl SECONDS] [--max-writes N]
              [--auth-cooldown SECONDS] [--load-wait SECONDS]
              [--http-timeout SECONDS] [--station NAME=URL]
              [--station-home NAME=PATH] [--niagara-home NAME=PATH]
              [--credential-env PREFIX] [--insecure-tls NAME]
              [--allow-tier-b NAME] [--allow-tier-c NAME]
              [--progress-file PATH] [--allow-http-for-tests]

Stdio MCP server for Niagara N4 stations (newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0). Run
the `mcp-n4` binary: starting it prints nothing and contacts no station. MCP
protocol versions: this server speaks 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05
(`server.protocol_versions` of the registry). A client asking for a newer
revision is answered with 2025-06-18. Only add a newer revision to that list
once its semantics (new message shapes, capabilities, required fields) are
implemented and tested here.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --allow-writes        register the write tools (dry run + confirmation token
                        each)
  --write-scope ORD_PREFIX
                        ORD prefix writes may touch (repeatable); none = no
                        writes
  --state-dir STATE_DIR
                        journal/audit directory (default
                        ~/.local/state/mcp-n4)
  --token-ttl SECONDS   confirmation token lifetime (default 300)
  --max-writes N        executed writes allowed per server process (default
                        200); a reconnect does not reset it
  --auth-cooldown SECONDS
                        after an authentication failure, refuse station calls
                        this long (default and minimum 30: the lock-out
                        window)
  --load-wait SECONDS   total wait for one component load (default 3; 1-60):
                        raise it for a slow or remote station
  --http-timeout SECONDS
                        HTTP timeout of one station request (default 20;
                        5-300)
  --station NAME=URL    station n4_connect may use (repeatable); NAME should
                        equal the station's stationName; URL must be https://
  --station-home NAME=PATH
                        directory holding the config.bog of configured station
                        NAME; lets n4_save_station prove persistence
                        (repeatable)
  --niagara-home NAME=PATH
                        Niagara installation directory of configured station
                        NAME, reachable from this machine (the one holding
                        security/licenses); lets n4_license_info add when
                        each licence was generated and its version
                        (repeatable)
  --credential-env PREFIX
                        env var prefix holding <PREFIX>_USER/<PREFIX>_PASSWORD
                        (default MCP_N4)
  --insecure-tls NAME   skip TLS certificate verification for this configured
                        station (self-signed); repeatable
  --allow-tier-b NAME   let writes run on configured station NAME although its
                        version is tier B (4.15/4.3); only after a PoC matched
                        that build (METHODOLOGY section 5); repeatable
  --allow-tier-c NAME   let writes run on configured station NAME although its
                        version is tier C (other or unknown); only after
                        reg.loadContract, loadRoot and a harmless scratch
                        write succeeded; repeatable
  --progress-file PATH  append JSON progress lines of long reads
                        (n4_inventory) to PATH
  --allow-http-for-tests
                        permit http:// base URLs (fake station in tests only)

read_tools.name: n4_connect
read_tools.description: Open a session to one of the stations the operator configured at server start (replaces any previous session). The URL, credentials and TLS policy are fixed by the operator and cannot be chosen here. The station's real stationName must equal expected_station (default: the configured station NAME), or the session is closed. With expected_version (e.g. 4.14 or 4.14.0.162), the detected version must equal it or start with it by whole dotted parts (4.14 matches 4.14.0.162, 4.1 does not), or the session is closed; an undetected version never matches. Reports the detected version (oBIX productVersion) and its tier: A (4.13/4.14) writes; B (4.15/4.3) and C (other or unknown) refuse writes unless the operator opted the station in.

expected_station.description: Required stationName; default: the station NAME

expected_version.description: Optional version the station must report: the full version or a dotted prefix (4.14 matches 4.14.0.162); a mismatch or an undetected version closes the session

read_tools.name: n4_describe_session
read_tools.description: Report whether a station session is active, which station, its version tier, and the server mode. Works without a session.

read_tools.name: n4_navigate
read_tools.description: List the children of a component (name, type, handle, has_children). depth > 1 nests grandchildren under a 'children' key. elapsed_ms is the load time. For a station inventory use n4_bql_query or n4_inventory instead: one navigate is one round trip per component. types (optional) keeps only children whose type is one of the given specs (e.g. bacnet:BacnetDevice) plus the path to them; each kept entry then carries matched true/false. has_children ignores the types filter: it is true when the entry has any component child, matching or not. types keeps a given type and its subtypes; types_note says when the registry could not be read. Each component or struct slot whose children are listed also lists the declared properties the station left out at their default (handle null), marked default: true with their value, or value null and a note when the type contract gives no default value; the sub-entries of a declared struct default are marked default too and may show type null. defaults_note says when a type contract could not be read, and names a declared default that could not be decoded (left out).

types.description: Optional type specs to keep, e.g. ['bacnet:BacnetDevice']; default: no filter

read_tools.name: n4_read_slots
read_tools.description: Read all slots of one component as {name, type, value, status}. Status complexes add status_ok/status_null; a Status slot's omitted value or status takes the type default. value_display carries the station's display string; a complex the reader cannot decode (e.g. a Modbus FlexAddress) returns that display string as value. elapsed_ms is the load time. A slot that is itself a baja:Status also adds status_flags, the names of the flags set; status_ok is false when any is set. A station leaves out a declared (frozen) property still at its default; those are listed after the loaded slots from the type contract (the station's type registry, read once per session), each marked default: true with the contract's default value, or value null and a note when the contract gives no default value (e.g. a component default such as proxyExt): never an invented value. defaults_note says when a type contract could not be read, and names a declared default that could not be decoded (left out). An ord that names a property of a component (a struct such as an alarm extension's toOffnormalTimes, a Status value, or a simple) lists that property's fields, or the property itself when it has none, and adds component_ord, property and property_type; an alarm:AlarmTimestamps adds alarm_timestamps {alarm_time, ack_time, normal_time (ISO with offset, null when unset), count}.

read_tools.name: n4_list_links
read_tools.description: List baja:Link / baja:ConversionLink links of components up to depth levels below ord. source_path is null when the source handle is outside the loaded subtree.

depth.description: Component levels below ord to scan (1-4)

read_tools.name: n4_find_dangling_outputs
read_tools.description: List components (up to depth levels below ord) with an 'out' slot that no link in the subtree uses as a source. Links from outside the subtree are not seen. A source ORD that is neither a handle nor an absolute slot path cannot be resolved: outputs it may feed are listed as unknown, not dangling. A component with an alarm or history extension child (alarm:...AlarmExt, history:...HistoryExt) has its out read by that extension without a link: it is listed in consumed_by_extension (with the extension type), not as dangling.

depth.description: Component levels below ord to scan (1-4)

read_tools.name: n4_bql_query
read_tools.description: Bulk read: one projected BQL select over a subtree, returned as rows (one HTTP GET, usually under a second, where a navigate crawl costs one round trip per component). Use it FIRST for any inventory. Only 'select <cols> from <type> [where ...]' is accepted; '|' is refused. The base may also be alarm: (the alarm database) or history:/<station>/<history name> (one history): there the query is 'select <cols> [where ...] [order by ...]' with no from clause, e.g. select timestamp, source, sourceState where sourceState = 'offnormal' order by timestamp desc, or select timestamp, value where timestamp.millis >= 1794808800000; same rows and columns, read-only. Columns are the station's display headers (e.g. 'Slot Path', 'Name'; a localized station translates them, a repeated header becomes 'Type#2'); the queried name column is decoded ($20 -> space), 'Slot Path' stays ORD-ready. Proxy-extension fields project as proxyExt.<slot>, e.g. proxyExt.dataAddress. Rows are capped (truncated=true when cut).

base.description: Subtree ORD or slot path, e.g. station:|slot:/Drivers (default: the station root); or alarm: for the alarm database, or history:/<station>/<history name> for one history (list ids with select historyConfig.id from history:HistoryExt)

query.description: select <columns> from <type> [where ...], e.g. select slotPath, name, out from control:ControlPoint; over the alarm: or history: base: select <columns> [where ...] [order by ...] with no from clause

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout in seconds

output_file.description: Optional plain file name (.csv or .json): the rows go to <state-dir>/bql/<name> (0600, never overwritten) instead of the reply

read_tools.name: n4_inventory
read_tools.description: Station inventory through three BQL queries: networks, devices and points below base (default /Drivers), counted per network and per device. A network's built-in local device slot (localDevice, e.g. SnmpNetwork's own agent) is flagged local=true and counted apart from field devices. progress lists each step's row count; the operator's --progress-file gets the same lines. A network is a driver:DeviceNetwork row at any depth, named by its path below base.

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per query in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_read_file
read_tools.description: Read one station file (e.g. a Px view file:^px/General.px) through the station's file servlet: GET /file/<path>. file_ord is a file:^ ORD or a path relative to the station home. Refused before any request: '..', '|', ':', absolute paths, directories, names ending in '.' or ' ' and .bog/.bog.gz (the station never serves them). Text types (px, xml, nav, chart, json, csv, html, txt, ...) return text; other files return size, sha256 and content type only (output_file saves the complete bytes under <state-dir>/files/). status is ok, forbidden (403: no read permission) or not_found (404); a 401 pauses station calls and is never retried. Reads are capped at max_bytes (truncated=true, sha256 null when cut).

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout in seconds

output_file.description: Optional plain file name with an extension: the complete bytes go to <state-dir>/files/<name> (0600, never overwritten)

read_tools.name: n4_list_px_views
read_tools.description: List the Px views (baja:PxView) below root with one BQL query: display_name, px_file (the file:^ ORD to pass to n4_read_file / n4_px_summary) and media. A PxView is a property value, not a component, so the station usually answers its slot path as NULL: slot_path and owner_path are null then (see owner_note).

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_px_summary
read_tools.description: Fetch one .px file (like n4_read_file) and summarize it without returning the XML: media, imported modules, canvases and viewSize, layers, widget and binding type counts, bound ORDs grouped by component (a trailing value slot such as /out stripped), images, included Px files, charts, other ORDs and label texts. Every list is capped at max_items. A file larger than max_bytes is refused, not summarized in part.

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_px_binding_audit
read_tools.description: Report the Px bindings whose ORD does not resolve (station-audits S15), read-only. Without file_ord it audits every Px view below root (the n4_list_px_views query, up to max_views), each relative ORD (slot:a, slot:../a, ../a) read against the component the view is on; with file_ord it audits that one .px file, relative ORDs read against base when given. A binding is the ord attribute of an element whose tag ends in Binding (ValueBinding, ActionBinding, kitPx and vendor bindings), widget being the nearest enclosing element with a name. Each distinct target is loaded once over BOX (a trailing |slot: hop dropped): one that loads resolves; one that does not is missing only when proven, i.e. its deepest ancestor that loads holds no slot by the next name, neither loaded nor declared by its type contract. Anything else is unknown with why, never counted as broken: another scheme (history:, file:, module:, ...), a chained ORD, a relative ORD with no base, a handle (h:) that does not load, a timeout or hidden station error whose parent still holds the name. Reply: views [{px_file, base, status (ok, not_found, forbidden, truncated, unparsable, no_file), bindings, error?}], broken and unknown [{px_file, widget, element, ord (as written), target (absolute ORD or null), why}], counts {views, bindings, unique_targets, resolves, missing, unknown} (per binding, except unique_targets), truncated (views past max_views or bindings past max_bindings were not audited) and elapsed_ms. One BQL read, one GET per .px file, then one load per distinct target and per ancestor walked. Read-only.

root.description: Slot ORD below which every Px view is audited (default: the whole station); ignored with file_ord

file_ord.description: Audit only this .px file: file:^px/General.px or px/General.px

base.description: With file_ord: the slot ORD relative binding ORDs are read against (the component the view is on), e.g. station:|slot:/Plant/AHU1

max_bindings.description: Most bindings audited across all views

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout in seconds of each .px read

read_tools.name: n4_list_batches
read_tools.description: List the write batches in this server's journal, newest first: batch_id, tool, station_name, ts, state (completed / in-doubt), verdict, rollback_of and rolled_back_by. Use it to find the batch_id for n4_rollback. A journal line that cannot be read is listed in unreadable and the reply says the list is incomplete. Reads the journal only; works without a session.

read_tools.name: n4_session_retro_draft
read_tools.description: Draft the session retro: reads this server's audit and journal and returns markdown plus evidence-backed CANDIDATE kit deltas (refusals, bad read-back verdicts, in-doubt batches, BOX errors, dangling outputs). Proposes only; never applies or stages anything. An audit line that cannot be read is named in the summary, which says the draft is incomplete. The window starts at the server start; pass since (ISO-8601, e.g. 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z for the whole history) to change it.

since.description: ISO-8601 timestamp; only newer entries are considered (default: when this server started)

read_tools.name: n4_spy_page
read_tools.description: Read one diagnostics page of the station's spy tree (GET /ord?spy:/<path>, the pages the Workbench Spy view shows) as data: title, tables (title, header, rows of cells), links to child pages as relative spy paths, the POST actions the page offers (named only as spy paths without their query, never invoked) and the text outside tables. The content of a form field (textarea, select, button, input) is never returned, wherever it sits. Read-only: one GET under the spy root. Refused before any request: a scheme or ':' (except one module:Type segment directly under sysManagers/registryManager/types/, the registry's type pages, e.g. sysManagers/registryManager/types/control:NumericWritable), '|', '..', a query string ('?', '&', '=', '#'), '%', ';', a backslash, any Unicode control character, invalid UTF-8 and the known action pages (util/gc, util/forceThreadDump). status is ok, forbidden (the user may not read spy pages), not_found, not_html or parse_timeout (the page was not parsed within timeout_s). Spy pages are diagnostics: their layout differs between Niagara versions, so read the tables as found. The reply is bounded as a whole: truncated is true when a cap cut it and truncated_by names the caps (max_bytes, max_rows across all tables, tables, row_cells, links, actions, name, cell, text).

path.description: Path below the spy root, e.g. metrics, sysInfo or util/JMX Info; empty for the index

max_rows.description: Cap of table rows returned, all tables together

max_bytes.description: Byte cap of the page read

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_station_health
read_tools.description: Station health in one call, each section answered on its own: system (the SystemService slots by their station names: CPU usage in percent, memory as the station reports it plus memory_used_percent, version, host, time), points (total, ok, null_only, not_ok_count, a count per status flag in by_flag and the not-ok ones in not_ok, up to max_not_ok; ok is no flag, null_only is the flag null alone, a point with no value and not a fault, and not ok is any other flag, so ok + null_only + not_ok_count = total; proxy is the points whose proxy extension is not control:NullProxyExt, the ones a licence counts), networks and devices (the same, plus disabled and each not-ok entry's name, type and enabled), totals (the n4_inventory totals of the same rows, with rows_truncated when a query feeding them was cut), capacity (resources: the Global Capacity table of the spy metrics page, per resource used and limit, unlimited true where the station shows no limit, and live; recount: its recount times) and elapsed_ms. Two counts sit side by side in a resource: used is the licence's own tally, the number to quote against limit for licensing, and it only grows until a capacity recount or a station restart; live is what the station really holds now (networks, devices and proxy points of the whole station; null for a resource this tool does not count or when base is a subtree). may_be_inflated is true, with an inflation_note, when a used is above its live or the recount has never run. A section that fails is {error} and the others still answer. capacity is null with a capacity_note when the spy metrics page is unreachable or holds no Global Capacity table: never a guessed count. capacity_truncated is true, and capacity_note says so, when the page was cut before it was read whole, so resources may be missing; rows of the table that do not match its header are counted in capacity_note. In a section, truncated means not_ok was cut at max_not_ok (not_ok_count is whole) and rows_truncated means the query hit max_rows, so the counts are lower bounds. A status the station did not answer counts under the flag unknown and as not ok, never as ok. license is the licence manager page (spy sysManagers/licenseManager) in short: licenses (name, expires, valid, with state when not valid, and days_left counted from the station's own date, the day of system.systemTime; null for never, for an expiry that is not a date or when that date is unknown; up to 100, licenses_count when more), nearest_expiry (the earliest dated expiry among licences, certificates and features, with same_date: how many share it), expired (what is already past; null when the station date is unknown) and a warning when the nearest expiry is 60 days away or fewer, or past, when a licence is not reported valid, or when an expiry could not be read as a date; note says what the reading could not do; {error} when the page was not read, saying which case it is (no permission, no such page, not HTML, not a licence page), never an empty licence. n4_license_info has the whole of it. drivers=true (default false; no extra request: it groups the rows of the networks, devices and points sections) adds drivers: per driver network {network (its slot path), name, type, status (its flags), enabled, devices, devices_bad, devices_bad_truncated, points, points_bad, points_bad_truncated}, and totals. devices counts the network's field devices (the local device left out) as total, down, fault, disabled (the disabled flag or enabled false) and unknown; points counts its proxy points (proxy extension not control:NullProxyExt; any other control point is no driver point and counts nowhere) as total, stale, fault, down, disabled and unknown. A status with several bits counts once in each of its categories, so the categories need not sum to total; unknown is a status the station did not answer as a number, never ok. devices_bad [{device, status, enabled false when so}] and points_bad [{point, status}] list the ones in any category, up to max_bad each (default 20), *_truncated true when cut. totals sums the networks and adds unassigned_points (proxy points under no network), proxy_unknown (points whose proxy type the station did not answer, not counted) and rows_truncated (a feeding query was cut: lower bounds). drivers is null with drivers_note when one of the three sections failed. platform=true (default false) adds platform: platform capacity and what is about to expire, each item null with a *_note saying why when it cannot be read, never a guess. heap {used_kb, committed_kb, max_kb, fraction, source}: used and committed are the JVM's totalMemory less freeMemory and totalMemory of the spy sysInfo page; max_kb is the sum of the defined maxima of the heap pools on spy util/JMX Info (null with max_note when it cannot be read), fraction is used_kb over max_kb. cpu {current, overall, cpus} and memory {total, free} repeat the system section (no request); the CPU usage slots hold -1 until the SystemService is polled, which its subscription by a load triggers, so the system section loads it once more when they are missing, and cpu is null with cpu_note (system.cpu_note too) when they stay unmeasured. history_db {histories, records, bytes, bytes_note, truncated, source}: the histories the spy localHistory page lists and their records summed; bytes is always null, no read-only page gives the size of the history files. licence {kind, name, expires, days_left, never_expires} is the license section's nearest expiry (no request); never_expires true when nothing on the licence page is dated. certificates lists the station's own key store certificates first ({alias, store station, expires, days_left, status}: one BOX load of Services/SecurityService/certificates, days_left the value of each entry's CertificateExpiryPoint and expires the station's date plus it), then the user and system trust store certificates of the spy securityInfo/Cryptography Info page ({alias, store, issued_by, expires, days_left}), each store nearest expiry first, up to 50, with certificates_count and certificates_note; null only when neither source answers. modules {count, truncated, items (only with include_modules), source} are the parts the spy module manager page lists. warnings lists a heap at 90% or more of its maximum, and the licence and each station or user certificate expired or expiring within expiry_warn_days (default 30) of the station's date; the system trust store (JDK roots) is one summary line, N system trust-store certificates expired or expiring (JDK roots; informational). Without platform the reply is unchanged.

base.description: Subtree ORD of the point, network and device counts, default station:|slot:/

drivers.description: Add drivers: devices and proxy points per driver network counted per down, fault, disabled and stale (no extra request)

expiry_warn_days.description: Window of the platform warnings: a licence or certificate expiring this many days away or fewer, or past, is warned about (with platform=true)

include_modules.description: List the loaded modules {name, vendor, version} in platform.modules (with platform=true; the count is always given)

max_bad.description: Cap of each network's devices_bad and points_bad lists (with drivers=true)

max_not_ok.description: Cap of the not-ok entries listed per section

platform.description: Add platform: heap, cpu, memory, history_db, licence, certificates and modules with expiry warnings (five more spy page reads and one BOX load)

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_read_history
read_tools.description: Read the last records of one history, newest first, to prove records arrive (a {ok} history extension proves it runs, not that records exist). Name the history by history_id (/<station>/<history name>, as historyConfig.id shows it) or by ext_ord (the history extension's ORD, e.g. station:|slot:/Folder/Point/NumericInterval, resolved to its id with one BQL select); give exactly one; a bare name (no '/') is a history of the connected station. Each row is {timestamp, value, status} as the station renders them (localized display text, e.g. '15 nov 2026 20:09:35 CST', '21,0', '{ok}'); columns are the station's headers. Optional range: period (today, last24Hours, yesterday, weekToDate, lastWeek, last7Days, monthToDate, lastMonth, yearToDate, lastYear) or start and/or end (BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000-06:00, or a span back from now such as 30m, 24h or 7d, sent as UTC; start no later than end), not both; range echoes the start/end sent. truncated is true when the range holds more records than limit; total_records is the range's record count (select count(*)), null with total_records_note when that count failed. summary=true answers how high (or low) it got in the same call: summary {count, complete, records_scanned, numeric, min {value, timestamp}, max {value, timestamp}, first and last {value, timestamp, status}, status_counts} over the WHOLE range whatever limit cut the rows, from one extra read of every record with machine-encoded time and value (timestamp ISO-8601 with the station's offset, value 21.0 not '21,0'; a tie keeps the earliest record). A non-numeric history (boolean, enum) has numeric false, min and max null and a note; a nan or inf record is counted but never compared. A range larger than summary_max_rows (default 100000) is summarized from its newest records with complete false, a note, and range_min/range_max from the station's select min(value), max(value) where status.null = false over the whole range (null-status records left out, as in the summary; a nan or inf record still counts there); a failed summary read is summary null with summary_note. A history that cannot be read is an error naming the id and how to list the ids. cov_hint=true (station-audits S3) suggests a COV changeTolerance from the same read (summary and cov_hint together still read once): cov_hint {suggested_tolerance, rule, records_considered, complete, deltas {count, median, p90, p99, nonzero_median, noise_floor, zero_share}, candidates [{tolerance, deltas_within, reduction}], reduction_estimate}. Rule: suggested_tolerance is the smallest value of the 1-2-5 series (..., 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, ...) at or above the nearest-rank median of the non-zero |delta| between successive records for which a simulated COV (keep a record when |value - last kept value| > tolerance, as BNumericCovHistoryExt compares) keeps at most half of the records; records with a null status or a nan/inf value are left out; noise_floor is the smallest non-zero |delta|. A non-numeric history (boolean, enum), fewer than 2 numeric records or a failed read is cov_hint null with cov_hint_note; a value that never changes has suggested_tolerance null and a note. Report only: nothing is written to the station. Read-only: fixed queries over a history: ORD, no file output (n4_export_history writes histories to a CSV).

history_id.description: History id /<station>/<history name>, e.g. /MyStation/MyPoint, or a bare history name of the connected station, e.g. MyPoint

period.description: Period id: today, last24Hours, yesterday, weekToDate, lastWeek, last7Days, monthToDate, lastMonth, yearToDate or lastYear

start.description: Range start as a BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000-06:00 or 2026-11-15T06:00:00Z, or a span back from now: 30m, 24h, 7d

end.description: Range end as a BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T23:59:59.999-06:00, or a span back from now: 30m, 24h, 7d

summary.description: true adds summary: count, min and max with their times, first, last and status counts over the whole range

summary_max_rows.description: Most records the summary reads; a larger range is summarized from its newest records and says so

cov_hint.description: true adds cov_hint: a COV changeTolerance suggested from the range's real data (report only, nothing is written)

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_export_history
read_tools.description: Export a range of one or more histories to ONE CSV file for client reports (station-audits S2). history_ids lists 1 to 20 ids, each checked like n4_read_history's history_id (/<station>/<history name>, or a bare history name of the connected station; anything else, '..', quotes and '|' included, is refused before any request). Optional range: period (today, last24Hours, yesterday, weekToDate, lastWeek, last7Days, monthToDate, lastMonth, yearToDate, lastYear) or start and/or end (BAbsTime or a span back from now such as 30m, 24h, 7d), not both; no range is the whole history. Each history is one read of select timestamp.encodeToString, value.encodeToString, status (machine-encoded: timestamp ISO-8601 with the station's offset, value 21.0 not '21,0'); the newest max_rows records of each (default 100000) are written oldest first. The server names and places the file: <state-dir>/exports/<station>-<UTC time>.csv (directory 0700, file 0600, never overwritten; the caller never passes a path). Columns: history_id,timestamp,value,status (header first, CSV quoting where a cell holds a comma, quote or newline, lines end in CRLF). Reply: path, rows_total, per_history [{history_id, rows, truncated}] (truncated: the range held more than max_rows records), bytes. A history that cannot be read stops the export with an error naming it, and no file is left. Reads the station only; the one write is that local file.

history_ids.description: 1 to 20 history ids, e.g. ["/MyStation/Temp", "Humidity"] (a bare name is a history of the connected station)

period.description: Period id: today, last24Hours, yesterday, weekToDate, lastWeek, last7Days, monthToDate, lastMonth, yearToDate or lastYear

start.description: Range start as a BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000-06:00, or a span back from now: 30m, 24h, 7d

end.description: Range end as a BAbsTime, or a span back from now: 30m, 24h, 7d

max_rows.description: Most records written per history (the newest of the range)

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_read_audit
read_tools.description: Answer who changed what on the connected station, in one call: the records of its audit trail (history /<station>/AuditHistory, written by Config/Services/AuditHistoryService), newest first, each {timestamp, operation, target, slot, old_value, value, user}: timestamp is ISO-8601 with the station's offset; target is the component's slot path as the station stores it (/Folder/Point, no slot: scheme); slot is the property or action name (a/b for a nested property); old_value and value are the station's text of the values (empty for an action or an added slot). Narrow it with target (a component ORD such as station:|slot:/Folder/Point; matches it and everything below it) or target_glob (a BQL like pattern over the stored slot path such as /Folder/*/Point; no quote, space, '$' or '|'), at most one; slot (exact slotName, e.g. overAmpsDelay); user (exact userName); operation (Changed, Added, Removed, Renamed, Reordered, Flags Changed, Facets Changed or Invoked; logins and recategorizations go to the security audit history instead); and either period or start/end (BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000-06:00, or a span back from now such as 30m, 24h or 7d). limit (default 100, 1 to 1000) caps the records returned. truncated is true when more records match than were returned; total_records is their count (select count(*) with the same filters), null with total_records_note when that count failed. The audit history keeps 500 records and rolls by default, so old changes may be gone. Every filter value is checked on its decoded form before any request. Read-only: fixed queries over the history: ORD.

target.description: Component ORD whose audit records to read, itself and below, e.g. station:|slot:/Folder/Point

target_glob.description: BQL like pattern over the stored target slot path, '*' any run of characters, e.g. /Folder/*/Point

slot.description: Exact slot (property or action) name, or a nested property path a/b, e.g. overAmpsDelay

user.description: Exact user name that made the change, e.g. admin

period.description: Named time range; or give start/end

start.description: Oldest record time as a BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000-06:00, or a span back from now: 30m, 24h, 7d

end.description: Newest record time as a BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T23:59:59.999-06:00, or a span back from now: 30m, 24h, 7d

limit.description: Most recent matching records to return

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_users_audit
read_tools.description: Audit the station's user accounts (station-audits S14), read-only and without a credential. One load of Services/UserService (each baja:User and its slots, two levels: an authenticator's own slots are never loaded), one of Services/RoleService and one fixed query of the /<station>/SecurityHistory Login records (where 4.x keeps logins; the AuditHistory does not). Fail closed: only fullName, enabled, expiration, lockOut, roles, authenticationSchemeName and prototypeName are returned; email and cellPhoneNumber show only "<set>" or "" under contact; every other slot (authenticator, password, permissions, vendor or dynamic slots) is never returned and is only named in masked_slots. Reply: users [{user, full_name, enabled, locked_out, expiration (null for never), roles, role_resolves, unresolved_roles, admin_role (a role that is baja:AdminRole or grants super), auth_scheme, prototype, last_login (null when no record), last_login_source (SecurityHistory, or null when it could not be read), contact {email, cell_phone}, flags (disabled, expired, locked, no_recorded_login, unused, admin, unknown_role)}], unused [{user, last_login}] (enabled users with no login within unused_days, claimed only when the records read reach back past the cut-off), unused_days, logins_since, counts (users and one per flag), masked_slots, notes, truncated (users past max_users) and elapsed_ms. A verdict the evidence cannot support is null, never guessed: role_resolves and admin_role need the RoleService; no_recorded_login means no Login record since logins_since (the oldest login record read; the SecurityHistory rolls, so an older login may be gone), and an empty history sets neither it nor unused. Read-only.

unused_days.description: An enabled user with no login in this many days is unused

read_tools.name: n4_histories_audit
read_tools.description: Audit the histories of the connected station below base, in one read-only call (station-audits S1). It lists: no_history, the control points with no history extension right below them ({point}), leaving out the points under slot:/Services unless exclude_services is false (services_excluded counts them); disabled, the history extensions whose enabled is false ({ext, history_id}); stale, the enabled histories whose last record is older than the larger of stale_factor x the collection interval and stale_min (interval histories; stale_min, default 10m, keeps short-interval histories whose records show up in batches from false positives) or than cov_max_age (COV histories), or that never recorded ({history_id, ext, last_record ISO-8601 or null, interval as a span such as 5m or cov, threshold, age, note}); near_capacity, the histories capped by record count holding at least capacity_warn of it ({history_id, ext, records, capacity, fraction, full_policy, severity, effect}: severity warning for full policy stop, where recording stops when full, info for roll, where the oldest records are overwritten); and colliding_ids, the history ids two or more extensions record into ({history_id, exts}). Each list keeps at most 100 items; counts holds the totals (points, history_exts and one per list). It reads select slotPath, type, enabled, historyConfig.id, historyConfig.capacity, fullPolicy, interval and lastRecord.timestamp (each as encodeToString) from history:HistoryExt (at most max_histories rows) and select slotPath from control:ControlPoint, then one select count(*) per distinct record-capped history id that has recorded (count_reads; requests is the total). truncated is true when a read stopped at its cap: then no_history is not checked (counts.no_history null, no_history_note says why). not_answered counts cells the station answered in no known form, per column; notes say what was left out. Read-only: fixed queries.

base.description: Slot ORD of the folder to audit, itself and below, e.g. station:|slot:/Drivers (default: the whole station)

exclude_services.description: Leave the control points under slot:/Services out of no_history

stale_factor.description: An interval history is stale when its last record is older than this many collection intervals

stale_min.description: Least age before an interval history is stale, whatever its interval: 30s, 10m, 1h (the threshold is the larger of stale_factor x interval and this)

cov_max_age.description: A COV history is stale when its last record is older than this span: 30m, 24h, 7d

capacity_warn.description: Fraction of a record-count capacity from which a history is near capacity

max_histories.description: Most history extensions read (and record counts read)

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_license_info
read_tools.description: What the station's licence manager says, in one call (one GET of the spy page sysManagers/licenseManager, read-only): host_id; certificates (name, expires, valid); licenses (name, expires, valid, days_left) with license_kind, the qualifier the page gives them (e.g. perpetual); brand, owner and project (the tridium:brand and tridium:about features); maintenance (below); nearest_expiry, the earliest dated expiry among licences, certificates and features (kind, name, expires, days_left, same_date: how many share that date); expired, what is already past (up to 50, expired_count when more); features (count, matched, list of name, expires and attributes by key, capped by max_features, truncated). valid is true only when the page writes the state valid; any other state is valid false with state, the text as written. expires is never, a date (YYYY-MM-DD) or, when the page writes anything else, that text as written with days_left null: such entries are counted in note and are in neither nearest_expiry nor expired. Every days_left counts calendar days from the station's own date (station_date, the day of the SystemService systemTime, which must be a whole timestamp), never this machine's: 0 on the expiry day, negative once past, null for never or when the station date is unknown (station_date_note says why, and expired is null). maintenance is what the licence states of the software maintenance agreement (SMA): sma_attributes, one entry per feature that has sma.* attributes (feature, attributes by key), up to 50 with sma_feature_count; sma_exempt_features, the names of the features whose sma.exempt is true, each once, up to 50 with sma_exempt_count (an exemption of that one feature, never of the licence as a whole); sma_truncated when a list was cut; feature, a feature named after maintenance when there is one; and expires, the end date of the agreement: null unless a local licence file states it, because the page carries none. The page does not carry when a licence was generated nor its version: only when the server was started with --niagara-home NAME=PATH for this station (its Niagara installation directory, reachable from this machine) each licence adds generated and version, and maintenance adds expires, days_left and license from the maintenanceExpiration attribute, all read from the root element of the file of that licence's name under security/licenses and nothing else of it (never its features or signature). Only a regular file of exactly the licence's name is opened; generated_note says, per licence, why the facts are missing: no such file, a link or another non-regular file, a name that differs in letter case, a file over 1 MiB or not a licence, one issued for another host, or past the 100 files read in one call. A local file that matches no licence of the page is neither read nor named. status is ok, not_recognized (the page answered but is no licence manager page), or a spy status: forbidden (the user may not read spy pages), not_found, not_html, parse_timeout; only ok carries the licence fields, so an unreachable page is never an empty licence. A line of the page is read whole or not at all: note counts the lines that matched no known pattern (two entries on one line, a name with a bracket or brace, a heading out of place) and names a cut page, a missing section and a list that was cut. The reply is bounded whatever the page holds: every string taken from the page is stripped of control characters and cut with the marker ...[cut] (200 characters for a name, expiry, state or host id, 64 for an attribute key, 100 for its value), a feature keeps 30 attributes (attributes_truncated), 100 certificates and 100 licences are read (certificates_count, licenses_count when the page has more), every list also stops at a byte budget, and the whole reply stays under 2 MiB for any page up to the 2 MiB read cap.

feature.description: List only this feature: an exact vendor:name (e.g. tridium:bacnet), else every feature whose name holds the text; compared without case

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_station_runtime
read_tools.description: What the station is running, in one read (read-only): uptime, from the spy page sysInfo: boot_time, current_time and up_time as the station writes them (localized text) and uptime_s, the seconds between its bootTicks and currentTicks; loaded_modules, from the spy page sysManagers/moduleManager, which lists only the module parts the station has loaded: count and modules (name, vendor, version), up to max_rows, truncated when cut; jars_on_disk: the session lists no module jars, so its status is unavailable (note says why) unless the server was started with --niagara-home NAME=PATH for this station (its Niagara installation directory, reachable from this machine): then the .jar files of PATH/modules (modules_dir, count; a link or other non-regular file is never opened and is named in skipped), with the root attributes of META-INF/module.xml read only from the jars that may hold a loaded part and from those changed after the boot (versions_read; jars whose module.xml cannot be read are named in unreadable; complete is false then or when the scan stopped at 5000 jars or timeout_s). mismatches (up to max_rows, mismatch_count, mismatches_truncated; null without the jars): module, reason, loaded_version, disk_version, jar and jar_modified, where reason is version_differs (the jar holds another version than the loaded one), modified_after_boot (same version, but the jar changed after the boot), loaded_not_on_disk (no jar holds the loaded part) or not_loaded_modified_after_boot (a jar of no loaded part changed after the boot). The boot is this machine's clock minus uptime_s, compared with the jar times of this machine's filesystem, with 2 s of slack. restart_needed is true with any mismatch, false only when the uptime, the whole loaded list and every jar are known and none differs, and null otherwise; restart_note says which. A spy page the user may not read is that section's status (forbidden, not_found, not_html, parse_timeout, with a hint), never a failed call; a page without the measured layout is not_recognized with a hint.

max_rows.description: Cap of the loaded modules and of the mismatches listed, each

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds; also bounds the reading of the jars

read_tools.name: n4_read_alarms
read_tools.description: Read the station's alarm records, newest first: by default the open ones (unacknowledged or not back to normal). Each row is {timestamp, uuid, source, source_state, ack_state, alarm_class, priority, msg_text} as the station renders them (display text, e.g. '7 nov 2026 09:20:50 CST', 'Offnormal', 'Unacked'; msg_text may be a raw %lexicon(...)% pattern; once back to normal the record holds the toNormal text) plus timestamp_iso, normal_time and ack_time as ISO-8601 with the station's offset (null when not set); columns are the station's headers. Filters, all optional and combined with and: source (a component ORD such as station:|slot:/Drivers/Net; matches it and everything below it), source_glob (a BQL like pattern over the stored source such as *slot:/Drivers/Net/D*, '*' any run of characters, an escaped one included; no quote, space, '$' or '|'), alarm_class (a class name such as defaultAlarmClass), source_state (normal, offnormal, fault, alert), ack_state (acked, unacked, ackPending), since and until (BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000-06:00, or a span back from now such as 30m, 24h or 7d). A source_state or ack_state filter replaces the open default; open_only false reads every record. where echoes the BQL where clause sent; truncated is true when more records match than limit; total is the matching record count (select count(*)), null with total_note when that count failed; state_counts=true adds state_counts {source_state {normal, offnormal, fault, alert}, ack_state {acked, unacked, ackPending}, records_counted, complete} counts every matching record per state (one more read, of the state tags), null with state_counts_note when that read failed. Every filter value is checked before any request, against its grammar and then as the station reads it ($xx / $uxxxx escapes decoded once, as BQL decodes them: one that decodes to a quote, space, '*', '|' or control character is refused): no quotes, wildcards or BQL of the caller reach the station. Read-only: fixed queries over the alarm: ORD.

source.description: Component ORD whose alarms to read, itself and below, e.g. station:|slot:/Drivers/Net

source_glob.description: BQL like pattern over the record source, '*' any run of characters, e.g. *slot:/Drivers/Net/D*

source_state.description: One of normal, offnormal, fault, alert; an empty string is no filter

ack_state.description: One of acked, unacked, ackPending; an empty string is no filter

since.description: Oldest alarm time as a BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000-06:00 or 2026-11-15T06:00:00Z, or a span back from now: 30m, 24h, 7d

until.description: Newest alarm time as a BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T23:59:59.999-06:00, or a span back from now: 30m, 24h, 7d

open_only.description: true (default) reads only open alarms (unacked or not normal) unless a state filter is given; false reads every record

state_counts.description: true adds state_counts: every matching record counted per source and ack state (one more read)

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_list_alarm_classes
read_tools.description: List the station's alarm classes with their priority per transition ({toOffnormal, toFault, toNormal, toAlert}, 0-255), whether each transition needs an acknowledgement (ack_required), their alarm counts, and the recipients each one routes to. Recipients are the alarm:AlarmRecipient components (console, email, station and others) and a class routes to one through a link from the class's alarm topic to the recipient's routeAlarm action; each class lists {path, type, link_name} of its recipients, recipients lists each recipient with the classes linked to it, and unresolved_links the routeAlarm links whose source is not a listed class. At most 50 recipients are read for links (recipients_truncated says when more exist). A value the station renders in another form is returned as its text. Read-only: two BQL selects at the station root and one tree load per class folder and recipient. audit=true (default false; no extra request) also answers "where do my alarms go": unrouted_classes lists the classes no recipient is linked to (with unrouted_note when a routeAlarm link is unresolved or recipients were left unread, since one of them may route it), audit_counts counts them, and each recipient gains settings, at_default, masked_slots and problems. settings fails closed: a value is returned only for an allowlisted slot of a known type (every recipient type: transitions, daysOfWeek, timeRange, routeAcks; email:EmailRecipient also to, cc, bcc, emailAccount, language; alarm:StationRecipient also remoteStation, lastFailureCause, status, persistent, retryInterval; alarm:ConsoleRecipient also status, defaultTimeRange); every other slot, and every slot of any other recipient type, reads '<set>' or '' and is named in masked_slots. to, cc, bcc and emailAccount of an email recipient and remoteStation of a station recipient read '' when the station omits them at their empty default, named in at_default. problems lists an email recipient with no address in to, cc or bcc or an address that is not an email, a station recipient with no remoteStation, empty transitions or daysOfWeek, an empty url, chatId or webhook slot, a last delivery failure, its text quoted only when lastFailureCause is allowlisted for the type; a problem never quotes a value off the allowlist. To create a class, see the README recipe (n4_create_component, n4_set_slot, n4_create_link).

audit.description: Add unrouted_classes, audit_counts and each recipient's settings and problems

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_event_report
read_tools.description: Report what happened during each alarm event of one source, in one call: per event (newest first) the alarm database times and the source's history over the event window, so 'how high did it get' needs no date arithmetic and no second tool. Name the alarms by source (a component ORD such as station:|slot:/Folder/Point/AmpsAlarm; matches it and everything below it) or source_glob (a BQL like pattern over the stored source such as *slot:/Folder/*; no quote, space, '$' or '|'); give exactly one; optional since and until (BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000-06:00, or a span back from now such as 30m, 24h or 7d) narrow the alarm time; max_events (default 10, 1 to 100) caps the events read. Every record is read, open or not: the alarm database keeps one record per event (one uuid), updated in place when the source returns to normal and when it is acknowledged. Each event is {uuid, source, alarm_class, transition, source_state, ack_state, alarm_time, normal_time, ack_time, acked_by, records, window, history, summary}: times are ISO-8601 with the station's offset (null when not set; acked_by is the record's user, null until acknowledged); window {start, end, end_is_now} is [alarm_time - margin_minutes, normal_time + margin_minutes] (default 15, 0 to 1440), up to now while the source has not returned to normal. history is the history read: history_id when given (a bare name is a history of the connected station) for every event, else the history extension on the alarm source's component (the alarm extension's parent) or on the source itself, found once per source with select slotPath, historyConfig.id from history:HistoryExt (history {id, found_by: history_id or history_ext, ext_slot, other_exts when several match: the first is read}). summary is n4_read_history's summary over the window: {count, complete, records_scanned, numeric, min {value, timestamp}, max {value, timestamp} (the peak and when; a tie keeps the earliest), first, last, status_counts}. No history found, a source that is not a slot path, or a failed read is history and/or summary null with summary_note on that event, never a failed report. truncated is true when more events match than max_events; total_events is their count (select count(*)), null with total_events_note when that count failed. Every filter value is checked before any request, as n4_read_alarms and n4_read_history check them. Read-only: fixed queries over the alarm: and history: ORDs.

source.description: Component ORD whose alarm events to report, itself and below, e.g. station:|slot:/Folder/Point/AmpsAlarm

source_glob.description: BQL like pattern over the record source, '*' any run of characters, e.g. *slot:/Folder/*

history_id.description: History to read for every event, /<station>/<history name> or a bare name of the connected station; default: the history extension beside the alarm source

since.description: Oldest alarm time as a BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000-06:00, or a span back from now: 30m, 24h, 7d

until.description: Newest alarm time as a BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T23:59:59.999-06:00, or a span back from now: 30m, 24h, 7d

margin_minutes.description: Minutes of history read before the alarm time and after the normal time

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_alarm_health
read_tools.description: How healthy the station's alarms are, in one call. A source stored as slot:/a or local:|station:|slot:/a is reported once as station:|slot:/a (the form the source filter of n4_read_alarms and n4_event_report takes). chattering (sources with at least chatter_threshold transitions in the window, most first, as {source, transitions, records}; each alarm record whose alarm time is in the window counts one transition out of normal, plus one back when its normal time is set), offnormal (sources with an open record not back to normal, once per source, oldest first, as {source, source_state, alarm_class, since, records}: since, state and class of its earliest such record), unacked_older (records not acknowledged whose alarm time is more than unacked_days days old, oldest first, as {source, alarm_class, ack_state, alarm_time, age_days}) and top_sources (every source of the window by record count, most first, as {source, count}). Each list is cut to top entries; counts gives the full numbers, truncated is true and truncated_note says which lists were cut or which read stopped at its 100000-record cap. window is a span back from now such as 30m, 24h or 7d. Read-only: two fixed BQL reads of the alarm: ORD (select source, normalTime.encodeToString where timestamp.millis >= <window start>; select source, sourceState.encodeToString, ackState.encodeToString, alarmClass, timestamp.encodeToString over the open records), grouped by the server; never a write. To act on a finding, read its events with n4_event_report or n4_read_alarms.

window.description: Span back from now the chattering and top-source counts cover: 1 to 5 digits and m, h or d, e.g. 30m, 24h, 7d

chatter_threshold.description: Transitions in the window from which a source counts as chattering

unacked_days.description: Age in days beyond which (strictly more than) an unacknowledged alarm is listed in unacked_older

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_refrigeration_faults
read_tools.description: Refrigeration fault rules over history data, report only (read-only). Each rule named in rules reads its histories over the window (period, or start/end as n4_read_history takes them; one GET per history, read once per call, ISO timestamps and locale-free values) and lists its findings as {count, items, more} (up to limit items, each with fact). Every threshold is an argument, with no default: sources disagree (a short cycle is a run under about 2 minutes for some and under 10 for others). short_cycling: runs of the compressor run history shorter than min_run_s (a run still on at the window end is not judged) and clock hours with more than max_starts_per_hour starts. defrost_termination: every defrost cycle classified by the highest coil temperature during it: ended by temperature (reached terminate_temp), by time (did not, and lasted at least max_minutes - slack_minutes; this is the finding), early, or open; cycles counts each. setpoint_not_reached: periods the room temperature stayed above setpoint + band for at least min_minutes (a sample holds until the next), skipping the periods exclude_history (for example the defrost) is true. over_amps: the clock hours with samples above limit, with the count and the peak. door_drift: door openings after which the room temperature rose more than max_rise above its value at the opening, looking until the door closed plus after_minutes. A boolean history counts true as on; a record whose status is null carries no value and is left out (null_records counts them). A rule whose history could not be read is {not_checked: why}, never clean; summary has one line per rule (ok, N finding(s), not checked: why); histories lists each read, in order, with records, null_records and truncated (more records existed: the oldest were cut; narrow the window or raise max_rows).

rules.description: The rules to run, each with its histories and thresholds

run_history.description: Compressor run (boolean) history id (/<station>/<name>, or a bare name of the connected station)

max_starts_per_hour.description: Most starts allowed in one clock hour

defrost_history.description: Defrost active (boolean) history id (/<station>/<name>, or a bare name of the connected station)

coil_history.description: Evaporator coil temperature history id (/<station>/<name>, or a bare name of the connected station)

terminate_temp.description: Coil temperature that ends a defrost

slack_minutes.description: A cycle within this of max_minutes counts as ended by time

temp_history.description: Room temperature history id (/<station>/<name>, or a bare name of the connected station)

exclude_history.description: Optional boolean whose true periods are skipped (e.g. defrost); history id (/<station>/<name>, or a bare name of the connected station)

amps_history.description: Compressor current history id (/<station>/<name>, or a bare name of the connected station)

door_history.description: Door open (boolean) history id (/<station>/<name>, or a bare name of the connected station)

temp_history.description: Room temperature history id (/<station>/<name>, or a bare name of the connected station)

max_rise.description: Largest acceptable rise after an opening

after_minutes.description: Minutes after the door closed still counted

period.description: A history period instead of start/end, as n4_read_history takes it (e.g. today, yesterday, last7Days)

end.description: Window end, BAbsTime; an event still open at the end is cut there

timeout_s.description: Read timeout per history, seconds

read_tools.name: n4_alarm_text_check
read_tools.description: Check the alarm source extensions below base for alarm texts that can never show what their author meant (kit rule LC9, build-n4-module-kit/types/logic.md; the live twin of bog-nav alarm-text, same rules and rows). The texts of a BAlarmSourceExt (toOffnormalText, toFaultText, toNormalText) are resolved against the alarm record, never the source, and every return to normal sets the record's msgText to toNormalText. Rules (each finding is {level: WARN, rule, path, slot, token, text}, in slot path order): parent-path, a %...% token rooted at no BAlarmRecord field (%parent...% or any source-slot path such as %out.value%; one row per token): use %alarmData.<key>%; empty-tonormal, toOffnormalText set with toNormalText empty, which blanks msgText on every return to normal (token and text empty); bad-format, a text BFormat cannot parse (a % that never closes, such as the lone % of 90% in Load at 90% of %parent.out.value%): it shows as "ERROR <text>" and none of its tokens is evaluated (one row per text, token empty): write %% for a literal percent. Tokens split as BFormat does: %% is a literal percent, a token ends at the next % outside parentheses. Not reported: %alarmData.<key>%, the other record fields (%sourceState%, %alarmClass%, ...), a function call such as %lexicon(module:key)%, and %%. alarm_extensions counts every extension read (BQL's from matches subtypes); bad_format counts bad-format rows and hint repeats the advice when there is one; summary is the one-line count (bad-format named only when present); truncated with note means max_rows or the byte cap cut the read and the counts are lower bounds. Read-only: one BQL select of slotPath and the three texts from alarm:AlarmSourceExt below base.

base.description: Subtree ORD to check, default the whole station (station:|slot:/)

max_rows.description: Row cap of the select (extensions read)

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_commissioning_report
read_tools.description: What is still wrong or unfinished below scope, in one call (read-only; about 11 station reads for the whole station whatever its size: one BQL query per table, one link scan, three slot loads and the licence page). The reply starts with summary, one line per section (ok / N finding(s) / not checked: why / skipped: why, with the truncation note), then requests (the station reads made) and each section: state (ok, findings, partial: clean in the checks that ran while others did not run, not_checked, skipped), findings (absent when no check ran) and checks. A check that ran is {count, items, more}: items are the first limit offenders as {path, name, fact} and more is how many the limit left out; a check that did not run is {not_checked: why} (a failed or impossible read: never a zero) or {skipped: why} (not asked for). Every fact is a value the station answered. points: the control points per status flag (in_fault, down, stale, disabled, overridden, in_alarm, null_output, status_unreadable); devices_down_or_disabled lists the devices that are down, disabled or in fault first, their points counted in their flags and not listed (under_listed_devices); networks_not_ok; by_network counts devices and points per driver network. histories: points_without_history (the points with no history extension below them: with expect_histories they are listed and are findings; without it the check is a count with the note pass expect_histories to list them, no list and not a finding), and the history extensions that are disabled, in_fault or never_recorded (lastRecord.timestamp null). alarms: points_without_alarm (only with expect_alarms), unknown_alarm_class (an alarm extension whose alarmClass names no class below Services/AlarmService), classes_without_recipient (no link from the class's alarm topic seen within three levels of the AlarmService), open_alarms and unacked_alarms (the classes with any, alarms is their sum). links (one scan link_depth levels below scope): unresolved_source (a source ORD that is neither a handle nor an absolute slot path, or a slot path that does not exist; source_outside_scan counts the sources not judged), inputs_with_several_links (a priority input in1..in16 targeted by more than one link), dangling_outputs (the check of n4_find_dangling_outputs; unknown counts the outputs it cannot decide). naming: duplicate_display_names among sibling points, escaped_names ($xx in the slot name), palette_default_names (a point of the control palette such as NumericWritable or BooleanPoint1, or a point called by the name of its own type plus the number the station appends, such as a kitControl:Tstat called Tstat1; a lone Tstat is not flagged). station (only when scope is the whole station): services_in_fault, licence_expiry (the warning of n4_station_health's license section), and unsaved_changes and last_backup, always not_checked with the reason: the station does not expose them to a read. Bounds: each query reads at most max_components rows; a truncated table sets truncated and truncated_note (truncated at N components: counts are lower bounds and absences are not asserted; narrow the scope), and a check that would assert an absence from it is not_checked; a link scan over max_components is not judged. spyder (only when asked in sections or with spyder_spec; one more query, two with spyder_spec): the download state of each Honeywell BACnet Spyder (select slotPath, name, enabled, deviceStatus, compileStatusFlag, sErrorStatus from honeywellBacnetSpyder:BacnetSpyder): disabled (Enabled=false, a Spyder left disabled after a download), device_status (deviceStatus other than 1), compile_status (compileStatusFlag other than 0), error_status (sErrorStatus not empty); spyders counts the Spyders read; io_mismatch (only with spyder_spec) compares each listed point's IOComp (select slotPath, SensorType, InputLow, InputHigh, OutputLow, OutputHigh, Terminal1 from honeywellSpyderTool:IOComponent) with the spec and lists the fields that differ, the points with no IOComp and the Spyders not found; a station without the Spyder modules answers the query with an error and the checks are not_checked.

scope.description: Slot path to report on, e.g. station:|slot:/Drivers/BacnetNetwork; default the whole station

sections.description: Sections to build; default all of them but spyder, which is added when spyder_spec is given

limit.description: Offenders listed per check (the count is always whole)

expect_histories.description: Which points should have a history extension: {kinds: [numeric, boolean, enum, string, writable], name_pattern: a glob such as *Temp* over the name or display name}, {} is every point; without it points_without_history is a count only

expect_alarms.description: Which points should have an alarm extension, same shape as expect_histories ({} is every point); without it points_without_alarm is skipped

spyder_spec.description: The IO each Honeywell BACnet Spyder should have, for the spyder section's io_mismatch: {<Spyder name>: {<point name>: {sensor_type, input_low, input_high, output_low, output_high, terminal}}} with names as Workbench shows them (e.g. {"2005": {"RA_T": {"sensor_type": 0, "terminal": 1}}}); numbers compare as numbers, texts ignoring case; given alone it adds the spyder section to the default sections; without it io_mismatch is skipped and only the download state is checked

link_depth.description: Component levels below scope the link scan reads (1-4); the scan loads link_depth + 3 levels of slots, so keep it low on a large scope

max_components.description: Hard cap of the rows read per query and of the components a link scan may hold

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_behavior_snapshot
read_tools.description: Snapshot the behaviour of the control points below scope before a module deploy, for n4_behavior_diff after it (read-only on the station). One BQL read: select slotPath, out.value, status.bits from control:ControlPoint (at most max_points rows). The result is written to <state-dir>/snapshots/<name>.json (0600, never overwritten: a taken name is refused) and the reply gives name, station, scope, taken_at, points, truncated (with truncated_note) and file. Values are kept as the station writes them (its locale included).

name.description: Snapshot name: letters, digits, '_' or '-', up to 80 (e.g. before_deploy_2026_11_16)

scope.description: Slot ORD whose control points are read

max_points.description: Most points read; beyond it the snapshot is truncated

timeout_s.description: Station read timeout in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_behavior_diff
read_tools.description: Compare a behaviour snapshot taken before a deploy (n4_behavior_snapshot) with a second snapshot, or with a live read of the same scope when after is omitted (that needs n4_connect), and list what changed: status_changed (status flags before and after, by name), value_changed (the out value text differs; with tolerance, two values that both read as numbers, a locale decimal comma and a trailing unit allowed, count as equal within it), missing (points gone) and new (points added), each as {count, items, more} with up to limit items, sorted by path; summary counts each and unchanged. When either side was truncated, missing and new are {not_checked: why}, never a zero. notes name a station or scope that differs between the two sides. Read-only.

before.description: Name of the snapshot taken before the change

after.description: Name of a second snapshot; omitted: read the live station now (same scope as before)

tolerance.description: Absolute difference under which two numeric values count as unchanged

max_points.description: Most points of the live read

timeout_s.description: Live read timeout in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_inventory_snapshot
read_tools.description: Snapshot the inventory of a subtree to a local file, for n4_inventory_diff later (read-only on the station). One BOX load of base: every component down to depth levels below it (at most max_components, beyond it truncated) with its slot path, type, handle and recorded slots. By default the recorded slots are the configured properties: the simple and Status values directly on the component (a Status as 'value {status}'), leaving out runtime state so two snapshots of an unchanged station diff to empty. The type contract decides, not the slot type (a writable's fallback is recorded): left out are slots flagged transient on the instance or in the contract (a point's out, the inputs other than in1 and in8, a history extension's lastRecord and status), a Status out its contract does not declare as configuration, and inputs a link drives; a component below a transient slot is left out with everything below it. When the contracts cannot be read, notes says so and only instance flags, Status outs and linked inputs count. slots names the slots to record instead. The file is written under <state-dir>/exports/ with a name the server makes (inventory-<station>-<UTC time>.json, 0600, never overwritten); the reply gives name, path, components, bytes, truncated, base, depth and notes.

max_components.description: Most components recorded; beyond it the snapshot is truncated

slots.description: Slot names to record instead of the configured properties (e.g. ["facets", "out"])

read_tools.name: n4_inventory_diff
read_tools.description: Compare two inventory snapshots (n4_inventory_snapshot) by slot path; reads only the two local files (no station request, needs no session). a and b are snapshot names as the snapshot reply gives them, files under <state-dir>/exports/: a name with '..' or a path separator, or one that is not there, is refused. The reply lists added and removed components [{path, type}], changed slot values [{path, slot, before, after}] (null: the slot was not sent, at its default or absent), type_changed [{path, before, after}] and handle_changed (informational: a re-created component), each cut to limit items (truncated says one was), counts of every list before the cut plus unchanged, and notes when the two sides differ in station, subtree, recorded slots or contracts, or one was truncated. Read-only.

read_tools.name: n4_list_schedule_kinds
read_tools.description: Which kinds of schedule a station can hold and how each works, so no type name has to be known (reads no station, needs no session). schedule_kinds: boolean, numeric, enum, string (weekly schedules with special events: out follows the weekly time ranges, special events override them, a default output fills the rest), calendar (a list of days other schedules reference) and trigger (fires a topic at times of day on chosen days); each with its station type, value_type, the plain value it takes, default_output, which parts it has (weekly, special_events, dates, times), purpose, behaviour and what its out is usually linked to (by convention a writable's in16). event_kinds: date, date_range, week_and_day, custom and reference (the days of a calendar), each with its type, purpose, whether a calendar can hold it (in_calendar) and its fields with their allowed values. Also priority (top special event first), cleanup (passed date and date-range events are deleted by the station) and export_import (the station types that copy schedules between stations; no tool here).

read_tools.name: n4_read_schedule
read_tools.description: One schedule decoded into plain JSON (one load; read-only), for every kind n4_list_schedule_kinds lists. kind and type; for boolean, numeric, enum and string schedules: out, next_time, next_value, default_output, in and facets (each value is {value, status}: value true/false, a number, an enum ordinal or a string, null when the status is null; status ok, null or the station's encoding), out_source (what drives out: Input, Special Event: <name>, Week: <day> or Default Output), effective (always, or the date range rule of the effective period), weekly (monday to sunday, each a list of {start, end, value} sorted by start, times HH:MM with end 24:00 for a range that runs to midnight; a range the station holds without a value is listed with value null and ignored true, since the station skips it) and special_events in priority order (name, kind, rule, priority 1 = highest, ranges). Rules by kind: date {year, month, day, weekday}, each "*" when it matches any; date_range {start, end} (two date rules); week_and_day {month, week, weekday}; custom {year, months, days, weeks, weekdays} (lists, empty = any); reference {calendar: the calendar ORD}. Months are jan..dec, odd, even; weekdays sunday..saturday; weeks week1..week5, last7days, calendarWeek1..calendarWeek6, before_last7/14/21. calendar: out, next_time, next_value and dates (name, kind, rule). trigger: enabled, times (HH:MM), dates, last_trigger and next_trigger. Every slot the station leaves out because it holds its default is filled from the station's type registry; a slot neither sent nor described is an error, never a guess. last_modified is the station's time of the last change.

ord.description: The schedule component's ORD, e.g. station:|slot:/Schedules/Lobby

read_tools.name: n4_schedule_audit
read_tools.description: Audit every schedule below base in one read-only call (station-audits S12): the boolean, numeric, enum and string schedules and the calendars (BQL select slotPath, knobCount from schedule:ControlSchedule; trigger schedules are not listed). schedules has one entry per schedule: {schedule (ORD), type, kind, out_value, next_time, next_value, special_events: {count, upcoming}, linked_targets, notes} (out_status too when out's status is not ok). out_value and next_value are plain values as n4_read_schedule gives them; next_time is the station's BAbsTime text, null when the station holds the null time (no next event). special_events.count is how many special events the schedule holds (a calendar: how many dates); upcoming lists those whose first day falls in the horizon from the station's date (SystemService systemTime), as {name, kind, date (YYYY-MM-DD), rule, ranges (start, end, value by time)} plus calendar for a reference event; it is null when the station's date could not be read. A reference event names a calendar: calendars lists each one {ord, resolves, why?} (resolves false when it does not load as a schedule:CalendarSchedule). A rule this audit does not evaluate (calendarWeek1..6, before_last7/14/21, a date range with other wildcards) is never guessed: it is left out of upcoming with a note. linked_targets is the schedule's knob count (BComponent.getKnobCount: the links that read it, from any slot; in practice out); unlinked lists the non-calendar schedules with none ({schedule}); calendars, referenced rather than linked, carry referenced_by (reference events in the audited schedules naming them) instead. If the station refuses knobCount, linked_targets and unlinked are null with a note. no_next_event lists the schedules whose next_time is the null time. A value that cannot be read is null with a note in that entry, never guessed; a schedule that cannot be loaded is listed under unreadable {schedule, error}. counts holds the totals (schedules, calendars, unlinked, no_next_event, upcoming_events, unreadable); truncated is true when the list stopped at max_schedules. One BQL read, one SystemService load, then one load per schedule and per referenced calendar outside the list. Read-only.

base.description: Slot ORD of the folder to audit, itself and below, e.g. station:|slot:/Schedules (default: the whole station)

horizon.description: How far ahead to list special events and holidays, in days from the station's date, e.g. 7d (1d to 366d)

read_tools.name: n4_read_tags
read_tools.description: Read the tags of one or more components (ord, or ords: up to 50). Per component: direct tags (metadata slots, as {id, namespace, name, type, value, slot, flags}; the slot name is the escaped id, hs:point is hs$3apoint), tag_groups (each an n:tagGroup relation to a group definition, {group_ord, slot}), direct relations ({id, endpoint_ord, inbound, slot}) and, unless implied is false, the implied tags the station's dictionaries compute ({id, type, value}; a tag group's tags appear here). relations: direct (default), all (adds the implied relations, such as n:parent and n:child) or none. One load per component, plus one session call each for implied tags and implied relations.

ords.description: Several component ORDs (1 to 50), read in order

implied.description: Also read the implied tags (default true)

relations.description: direct (default): the relation slots on the component; all: also the implied relations; none: no relations

read_tools.name: n4_neql_query
read_tools.description: Find components by their tags with a NEQL query (one GET of base_ord|neql:<query>|view:file:ITableToCsv, the documented ORD route). neql is a filter such as n:point, hs:equip and not hs:ahu, tst:label = "hello", hs:temp > 20, n:name like ".*Pump.*" or a relation path (n:parent->hs:floor = 2); implied tags count.
