It matches the components below base_ord (default station:|slot:/), never base_ord itself, and returns their station ORDs (ords). With bql (one select, e.g. select slotPath, out.value) the station runs that select on the matches and the reply carries its columns and rows instead. '|' is refused (the ORD separator); a query the station cannot parse is HTTP 400, reported as such. max_rows (default 200, at most 2000) bounds the reply; truncated says it was cut.

neql.description: NEQL filter, e.g. hs:point and hs:temp

base_ord.description: Search below this component ORD (default station:|slot:/)

bql.description: Optional select run on the matches, e.g. select slotPath, out.value

timeout_s.description: Request timeout in seconds (default 60)

read_tools.name: n4_semantic_export
read_tools.description: Export the Project Haystack (hs:) tags of the components a NEQL query matches as a Haystack grid in the Haystack 4 JSON encoding (Hayson), read-only. One NEQL GET finds the components (default neql: hs:site or hs:space or hs:equip or hs:point; base_ord as n4_neql_query takes it), then each is read as n4_read_tags reads it (one load, plus one impliedTags call unless implied is false). Each row has id (a ref made from the slot path with its $-escapes decoded: '/' as '.', any character a Haystack ref does not allow as '_', ~2, ~3 on a clash), dis (hs:dis when set, else the decoded slot name), every hs: tag with the namespace stripped (marker, number, bool, string) and every outbound hs: relation as a ref (to the row's id when its endpoint, by slot path or h:<handle>, is exported too). Tags of other namespaces are left out; a value that cannot be converted is listed in skipped with why, never dropped silently. truncated says the NEQL match list was cut at max_entities. With save_as the grid is written as <state-dir>/exports/<save_as>.json (mode 600, never over an existing file) and the reply carries path and bytes; without it the reply carries the grid. Brick output is not produced.

neql.description: NEQL filter of the components to export
neql.default: hs:site or hs:space or hs:equip or hs:point

implied.description: Also export implied tags (one impliedTags call per component)

save_as.description: Write the grid to <state-dir>/exports/<save_as>.json instead of the reply (letters, digits, _ and -, up to 80)

timeout_s.description: NEQL read timeout, seconds

read_tools.name: n4_list_tag_dictionaries
read_tools.description: List the tag dictionaries installed under the TagDictionaryService (one BQL query), each with its namespace, enabled, frozen, version and status, and what it defines: tag definitions (id, info type, value type, default, validity condition; type null for a smart tag the station computes), tag groups (id, the group_ord a tag group relation points at, the tags it implies) and relation ids. dictionary (a name such as Niagara, or a namespace such as n) lists one. max_items (default 200, at most 2000) bounds the definitions listed across all dictionaries; truncated says some were left out. Use it before n4_set_tags to see which tags, values and groups a station defines.

read_tools.name: n4_tag_coverage
read_tools.description: Report how far the Haystack tagging below base reaches, in one read-only call (station-audits S9). points_without_tags lists the control points missing hs:point (a direct or implied marker) or an outbound hs:equipRef relation (direct, or implied when the client can call the session handler) as {point, missing: [hs:point, hs:equipRef]}; the ORDs feed n4_set_tags ords. equips_without_points lists the hs:equip components (NEQL hs:equip, implied tags included) that no point read names in an hs:equipRef, by handle (h:5) or slot ({equip}); it is null with a note when the points or equips were not all read. unknown_tags lists the direct tags of those points and equips that no installed dictionary defines ({tag, count, example, why}, most frequent first); the tags of a namespace no dictionary installs are ONE entry ns:* (why: no dictionary installed for namespace ..., ad hoc tags), so a station without a Haystack dictionary says so once. dictionary limits the check to one installed dictionary (name or namespace). Points under slot:/Services are left out unless exclude_services is false. Each list keeps at most 100 items; counts holds the totals (points, equips, points_without_tags, missing_point_tag, missing_equip_ref, equips_without_points, unknown_tags, services_excluded, unreadable). truncated is true when a read stopped at max_points. It reads select slotPath from control:ControlPoint, neql:hs:equip, the dictionaries under TagDictionaryService, then one load per component plus, for points, one impliedTags and one impliedRelations call (implied_unavailable when the client cannot). A component that cannot be read is listed under unreadable. Read-only.

base.description: Slot ORD of the folder to audit, itself and below, e.g. station:|slot:/Drivers (default: the whole station)

dictionary.description: Name or namespace of the one installed dictionary to check tags against (default: all installed)

max_points.description: Most control points read, and most equips

exclude_services.description: Leave the control points under slot:/Services out

write_tools.name: n4_create_component
write_tools.description: Add a component under parent_ord (optionally with a wire sheet position). Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

name.description: Requested slot name (the station may rename on collision). A display name the station stores escaped (a leading digit, a space) is created under its SlotPath escape and the plan says so: 2012 is stored as $32012

wire_sheet.description: Optional {x, y, w} wire sheet annotation (integers; w defaults to 8)

proxy_ext.description: Optional driver proxy extension type spec (e.g. modbusCore:ModbusClientNumericProxyExt) to create a point with; configure its address afterwards with n4_set_slot

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_add_history
write_tools.description: Add one history extension per point, already configured: historyName (baja:Format pattern), enabled and, for mode interval (the default), interval (ms), in one batch under one confirmation token (1 to 50 points). Mode cov adds a change-of-value extension instead, which records each change of the point value and has no interval. The extension type follows the point type read from the station (numeric, boolean, enum or string control point: NumericInterval / NumericCov, BooleanInterval / BooleanCov, EnumInterval / EnumCov, StringInterval / StringCov), and so does its default slot name. Refuses a point that is not one of those, an ext_type that does not fit the point, a point that already has a child named ext_name and, when the pattern only uses %name%/%parent...name% tokens, a history id (/<station>/<history name>) that would repeat in the batch or that an extension on the station already holds (one BQL read). The capacity argument sets the history capacity in records or unlimited, and full_policy (roll, the default, or stop) what happens when it is reached, each by a set op on historyConfig right after each add in the same batch; without them the extension defaults stay (500 records, roll). change_tolerance sets changeTolerance of a numeric change-of-value extension in its add body, and is refused for mode interval or a point that is not numeric. The plan notes how long the capacity lasts at the interval. The read-back checks the type, the configured slots, the capacity, full policy and change tolerance when given, the history id and that the extension is not in fault. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

points.description: Point ORDs (1 to 50), each gets one extension

history_name.description: baja:Format pattern for the history name, unique per device, e.g. S%parent.parent.parent.name%_%parent.name%

interval_ms.description: Sampling interval in milliseconds (300000 is 5 minutes); required for mode interval, refused for mode cov

mode.description: interval: sample every interval_ms; cov: record each change of value (no interval). Default: the mode of ext_type when given, else interval

capacity.description: History capacity: a number of records (the oldest roll off when full; 20160 is 7 days at 30 s) or "unlimited". Default: the extension default, 500 records

full_policy.description: What the history does when the capacity is reached: roll drops the oldest record, stop stops recording. Default: the extension default, roll

change_tolerance.description: Mode cov on numeric points only: the smallest change of the point value that records a new record, in the point's units (changeTolerance of NumericCov). Default: the extension default, 0

ext_name.description: Slot name of the extension under each point; default: the extension type's short name, e.g. BooleanInterval

ext_type.description: History extension type; default: the one that fits each point's type, and a type that does not fit is refused

enabled.description: Start collecting at once (true) or leave disabled

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_add_alarm
write_tools.description: Add one alarm extension per point, already configured, in one batch under one confirmation token (1 to 50 points). Every palette alarm extension is an alarm:AlarmSourceExt whose offnormalAlgorithm and faultAlgorithm follow its kind: out_of_range (numeric point: high/low limits, deadband, limit texts, and fault limits on its faultAlgorithm; giving a limit enables it), numeric_change_of_state (numeric: alarm_values), boolean_change_of_state (boolean: alarm_value), boolean_command_failure (boolean), enum_change_of_state and enum_command_failure (enum: alarm_values for change of state), string_change_of_value (string) and status (any control point). Without kind, the point type read from the station picks it: numeric out_of_range, boolean boolean_change_of_state, enum enum_change_of_state, string string_change_of_value. Each extension is added with its plain slots (alarmClass, sourceName, toOffnormalText, toFaultText, toNormalText, timeDelay, timeDelayToNormal, hyperlinkOrd), then set ops in the same batch swap both algorithms by type and set alarmEnable, alarmInhibit and the algorithm slots by path. Texts are baja:Format patterns resolved against the alarm record: %alarmData.sourceName%, %alarmData.presentValue%, %alarmData.highLimit%, %alarmData.lowLimit%, %lexicon(module:key)%, %% for a literal percent; %parent...% does not resolve in the state texts (it does in source_name). Refuses a kind that does not fit a point (naming the kinds that do), an algorithm argument the kind does not take, an alarm_class the station does not hold (one BQL read; the refusal lists the existing classes), a child already named ext_name and a second extension of the same kind on a point unless allow_second. The read-back reads every slot it set and both algorithm types, and lists under coerced each slot the station stored differently ({slot: {sent, read}}, verdict mismatch). Alarm recipients, routing and acknowledging are other tools' work. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

points.description: Point ORDs (1 to 50), each gets one alarm extension

kind.description: Alarm extension kind; default: the one that fits each point's type (numeric out_of_range, boolean boolean_change_of_state, enum enum_change_of_state, string string_change_of_value); a kind that does not fit is refused

ext_name.description: Slot name of the extension under each point; default: the palette name of the kind, e.g. OutOfRangeAlarmExt

high_limit.description: out_of_range: offnormalAlgorithm/highLimit; giving it sets limitEnable/highLimitEnable true

low_limit.description: out_of_range: offnormalAlgorithm/lowLimit; giving it sets limitEnable/lowLimitEnable true

high_limit_text.description: out_of_range: baja:Format text of a high-limit alarm; it overrides to_offnormal_text, e.g. %alarmData.sourceName% high: %alarmData.presentValue% > %alarmData.highLimit%

write_tools.name: n4_copy_component
write_tools.description: Copy one configured component (e.g. a Modbus device with its points and their addresses) under the same parent once per new name, in one batch under one confirmation token (1 to 30 copies). The copy holds the type, plain slots and child components up to 6 levels deep. Runtime slots are left out by flags read from the station's type definitions: a frozen slot declared readonly, transient or default-on-clone (e.g. status, health, out, read and write values) or made transient, and a dynamic slot flagged transient or remove-on-clone; flags an integrator set otherwise travel with the copy. The plan notes list each slot left out with its flags, calling out a readonly slot that holds a non-default value; actions, slots the station lists by name only and links are not copied either; a deeper source is refused. The read-back compares each copy's whole configured subtree with the plan. The source may carry station escapes (Numeric$20Writable40001); new names are plain. A Modbus device allows one writable point per register: a copy of a writable Modbus point keeps its source's address, so the station resets it to Hex:-1 ("Duplicate Writable point for register address"); give each such copy its own proxyExt/dataAddress with copies[] (applied in the same add, so the read-back can verify it). The plan notes such copies and the read-back names the cause. The plan also notes every writable point with a non-null fallback: each copy commands its device with it on first communication. Change what else differs per copy afterwards (e.g. deviceAddress with n4_set_slot). Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

Per target, copies[] gives a point's copy its own name and/or proxyExt/dataAddress (applied in the same add). Every add spends one write of --max-writes: the plan notes the count and a replication larger than write_budget.remaining is refused before any token is issued (n4_save_station stays outside the budget). A child that already exists under a target with a copy's name is refused. The plan notes copies of writable Modbus points that would share a register on one device (the station resets the later one to Hex:-1) and every writable point with a non-null fallback (each copy commands its device with it on first communication). The read-back compares every copy's configured subtree with the plan; the inverse removes every copy. write_tools.name: n4_set_schedule
write_tools.description: Change the weekly schedule, the default output, the special events, a calendar's dates and a trigger's times of a schedule in one batch under one confirmation token. weekly {day: [{start, end, value}]} replaces only the days given (monday..sunday; the days not given keep their ranges; {"sunday": []} clears one): times HH:MM, end 24:00 for midnight, start inclusive and end exclusive. default_output sets the value out takes when nothing is active (null: a null status). add_special_event [{name, kind, rule, ranges}] adds events with the kinds and rule fields of n4_list_schedule_kinds and n4_read_schedule (date, date_range, week_and_day, custom, reference); remove_special_event [names] removes events; an event is replaced by removing and adding it in one call. The events keep their order, which is their priority, and new ones go last. A date or date range that ends before today can never occur again and is refused unless allow_expired is true. add_date [{name, kind, rule}] (date, date_range, week_and_day or custom) and remove_date [names] change the dates of a calendar or of a trigger; a date is replaced in two calls. times [HH:MM] replaces a trigger's firing times. Values follow the schedule kind: true/false (boolean, calendar), a number (numeric), an ordinal of the range facet (enum), a string (string). Before anything is sent every fault is named, one message each: an unknown day, a malformed time, an end not after its start, overlapping ranges in a day, a missing value or one of the wrong type, a part the kind does not have (a calendar or trigger has no weekly schedule, a trigger no default output). Each day, the default output, the special events list and the times is one set that replaces it whole, a date one remove or one bare add then a set of each of its parts, so the inverse restores the previous schedule exactly (n4_rollback). The read-back reloads the schedule and compares each part written with n4_read_schedule's view of it. The station recalculates out, next time and next value by itself. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

write_tools.name: n4_ack_alarm
write_tools.description: Acknowledge alarm records, chosen either by uuid (uuids: 1 to 100, as n4_read_alarms returns them) or by a selection (select: {source?, alarm_class?, before?, max?}), with optional notes, through the station's alarm channel (ackAlarms): the station sets the acking user, the ack time and ackState ackPending, updates the alarm database and routes the ack. Give exactly one of uuids or select. A selection reads only unacknowledged records with the same records query n4_read_alarms uses, newest first: source is a component ORD (station:|slot:/a, slot:/a or local:|station:|slot:/a) matching the record source exactly or below it in both stored spellings, alarm_class a class name, before a BAbsTime or a span back from now (24h) selecting records at or before it, max at most 100 (default 100); at least one of source, alarm_class or before is required. The dry run resolves the selection to exact uuids and returns them in plan.selection.records as {uuid, source, alarm_class, timestamp}, with matched (the count of matching records) and truncated (more matched than max); the confirmation token is bound to that exact list, so executing acknowledges those uuids and never re-runs the selection (an alarm raised after the dry run is left alone; execute without the matching dry run is refused). A selection that matches nothing is a dry run with no token. The dry run reads each record first and refuses, naming them, any uuid with no record, any record whose source is outside the write scope (or is not a slot path), and any record already acknowledged or ack pending. The read-back re-reads the records: verified when none is still unacked and each has a user; mismatch when any stayed unacked or the station names alarm classes the user may not acknowledge (it needs operatorWrite on the record's class; those names are returned in observed.permission_failed_classes). An acknowledgement cannot be undone: there is no inverse and n4_rollback cannot reverse it. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

write_tools.name: n4_set_tags
write_tools.description: Add, change or remove direct tags on 1 to 50 components (ords) in one batch. add: [{id, value?, type?}] where id is ns:name; a tag the installed dictionaries define takes the definition's value type (a type that differs is refused) and, without value, its default; a Marker takes no value. A tag no dictionary defines is refused unless allow_ad_hoc is true, and never allowed in an installed dictionary's namespace (the Tagging guide: an ad hoc tag must not use an existing dictionary's namespace). A new tag is added as a metadata slot (flag m, named ns$3aname); a tag already there with another value of the same type is set (a type change is refused: remove, then add); one already holding the value is skipped with a note. remove: [id] removes direct tags (the inverse re-adds each with its type, value and flags). add_groups / remove_groups: [id] apply or remove a tag group an installed dictionary defines (a relation n:tagGroup to the group's definition, flag r, as Workbench adds it); the station then implies the group's tags, and the read-back lists the target's implied tags and any group tag missing from them. add_relations / remove_relations: [{id, endpoint_ord}] add or remove an outbound relation to another component (written as its handle ORD h:...), the id defined by a dictionary or, with allow_ad_hoc, in a namespace of its own. A group or relation already on the target, one missing from a remove, an entry named twice, or one both added and removed is refused. At most 200 ops (targets x changes), each target under the write scope. The read-back reloads each target and reports values the station normalized under coerced (sent 4.50, stored 4.5). It removes tags and relations, so it is in the destructive class (destructiveHint). Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run; n4_rollback undoes the batch.

add.description: Tags to add or change: [{id: "ns:name", value?, type?}]

allow_ad_hoc.description: true allows a tag or relation no installed dictionary defines, in a namespace no dictionary installs

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)
